reasons: F01, F03, F04, F05, F06, F07, F14, F15, F16, F17, F18, F19: clean governance and control profile: no material weakness, unqualified ICFR opinion, no going concern, no auditor or CFO/CEO turnover, no restatement, no investigations, litigation or covenant problems.

R08, R10, R19: total and RSST accruals are negative (-0.10) and the negative CFO/NI ratio (-7.74) most plausibly reflects a net loss alongside positive operating cash flow, so cash earnings exceed reported earnings, which argues against income inflation.

R09, R17, R01, R11, R18: Beneish M-score (-3.1) well below the -1.78 threshold and Dechow F-score (0.43) below 1.0; receivables are shrinking faster than sales (DSRI 0.84, AR growth minus sales growth -0.13), with no sign of channel stuffing (F10).

R04, R02, R06, R15, R05: sales fell about 20% with gross margin deterioration (GMI 1.28), SG&A rising relative to sales (SGAI 1.5) and ROA dropping 0.12, a stressed operating picture that raises pressure to manage results; the slowing depreciation rate (DEPI 1.39) could indicate useful-life assumptions being stretched.

R13, F24, F28: soft assets make up 77% of total assets and goodwill/intangibles is the critical audit matter; together with a segment/reporting change during a downturn, this creates judgment risk around impairment timing and reporting-unit allocation.
F26, F21, R16: emphasis on non-GAAP measures and a capital raise in the year or planned add some incentive to present results favourably, though R16 shows no securities issued in the ratio data.

F08, F09, F11, F12, F22, F23, F25, F27: low-risk revenue profile (point-in-time recognition, no significant contract assets), no material related-party transactions, moderate customer concentration (12%), no major acquisition, SPAC or voluntary accounting change, and no significant inventory writedowns.
